text: Type 2 diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic disorder characterized by persistent hyperglycemia and impaired insulin action. Diagnosis uses validated plasma glucose or glycated hemoglobin testing. Long-term care includes monitoring cardiovascular and renal risk.

Glycated hemoglobin, commonly called HbA1c, reflects average blood glucose exposure over roughly the previous two to three months. Laboratory interpretation should follow the reference method and clinical context.
Diabetic kidney disease may present with albuminuria and declining estimated glomerular filtration rate. Monitoring kidney function and cardiovascular risk is part of chronic diabetes care.

Hypertension is defined by persistently elevated blood pressure measured with validated technique. Management combines lifestyle measures with antihypertensive medication when indicated by overall cardiovascular risk.
Iron deficiency anemia can result from inadequate iron intake, impaired absorption, or chronic blood loss. Evaluation commonly includes hemoglobin, ferritin, and a search for the underlying cause.
